decisions.topic: A pending plan payment never traps the business (HY1, HR1, HU6)
decisions.decision: HY1: GET /v1/business/plan (E-27) gives `pending` as {reference, plan, startedAt, lapsesAt}: lapsesAt is when the waiting plan payment lapses (60 minutes after it started). GET /v1/payments/:reference (E-88) also answers a plan payment of the caller's business for everyone who may pay for the plan (the owner and a live login of the business, as HH6 has it), whoever started it; another business's plan payment is 404. POST /v1/business/plan/pending/:reference/drop drops the business's waiting plan payment at once: the owner only (a login is 403 with words), the payment becomes abandoned, one audit row is written as the business's own act (actor account, section /business/plan), and the answer is the plan read, so a new start is allowed. The same payment dropped again answers the plan read and writes nothing more; a payment that was paid, failed or refunded is 409 plan_payment_not_waiting with words; a reference of another business is 404. A late `paid` for a dropped payment follows HU6: it is fulfilled only if nothing else has paid for a plan of that business since (any payer of the business), otherwise it is marked refund due (refund_due:paid_after_drop, with words on the payment read). The drop is one conditional statement on the payment row and the settle holds that row, so a drop and a settle at the same moment give one outcome.

decisions.topic: Staff Support and Concierge lists take a search word (HY2)
decisions.decision: HY2: GET /v1/admin/support/threads (E-206) and GET /v1/admin/concierge/orders (E-37) take `q` (trimmed, 1 to 100 characters, a plain word: % and _ match themselves) beside cursor and limit, and Support keeps its status and assigneeId filters. Support matches a thread's subject, the name of the person, the thread's email address and a wish number of the person's account (case blind, part of a word); Concierge matches the order's id (the order number is the start of the id), the name and the email of who ordered, the business name and the names of the receivers on the wishes delivered for it. The match is made on the stored values and the role's masking is applied to what comes back, so a search by a full address finds the thread and returns the masked address; a word that matches nothing is an empty page, never an error. Paging by cursor holds with q.

decisions.topic: A short staff list for a hand-over (HY3)

GET /v1/admin/team stays owner only.

decisions.topic: The Concierge order carries its payment (HY4)

Nothing of the buyer's other wishes in any state, made alone or for a business's clients: a buyer with none delivered gets an empty list, and the maker sees no wish before it is delivered. A maker reads only an order given to them: another maker's order and an unknown order are 404.

A payment started after the first was fulfilled is a new intent and adds a month (HR1). A pack is not a plan. HZ4: a plan-payment start (purpose pro_plan) naming the pack is 422 with words. Response shapes: E-269 answers the plan read (E-27, whose pending is {reference, plan, startedAt, lapsesAt}), E-270 answers {items: [{id, no, firstName}], nextCursor: null}, E-271 answers {items: [{id, name, role}], nextCursor: null}.

decisions.topic: One call sends a reveal; a reveal's passcode holds for every link (IA1, IA4)
decisions.decision: IA1: POST /v1/business/reveals (E-272) takes the E-33 reveal body plus the client wish's own fields (client, kind, occasion, day: each defaulting from the reveal) and an Idempotency-Key, and in ONE transaction under the owner's lock makes the client wish (taking one wish from the month's allowance or the pack, as E-30 does), the reveal link, the shoot's mark and the one email, or none of them: a refused email (429 over the day's limit, 422 for a bad address), an empty pack (402 no_wishes), a file the set does not hold (422) or another business's shoot (404) leaves no wish, no link and no draw. The same Idempotency-Key answers the first result and sends nothing (30 identical calls make one wish). A shoot already revealed on that set to a client of the same name (compared without case or extra spaces) answers 409 already_sent whose fields carry sentAt and link, unless the body says `again`: then the reveal is sent again on the same client wish, taking no second wish. The answer is {shoot, wish, link}. E-30 and E-33 keep working as before. IA4: a link the business copies for a shoot's set (E-153) carries the passcode of the newest live reveal sent on that set; sending a reveal with a passcode gives the passcode to the links already copied for that set; so copying a link never gives a way in without the passcode.

IB1: GET /v1/r/:code/favourites (E-275) and POST /v1/r/:code/favourites (E-276, body {position, marked}) with no account, past the passcode where the reveal has one (403 passcode_required with words before it; 410 for a link switched off or ended). Marks belong to the link: positions in the link's file list (RevealPlay.index), up to 200, the same mark twice changes nothing, 60 marks an hour for a link and address (429, PROVISIONAL), one transaction with the writes below. The business reads them: RevealLink.hearts (E-152), the client wish's `hearts` (the positions) and the shoot's `hearts` (the file ids marked at any of its links); it cannot change them. Sending the reveal again with other files starts the marks over. RevealPlay carries `hearts` so the player starts with them.

IB2: RevealPlay (E-248) carries `downloads`, one {name, url} (a signed address, ten minutes) for each photo in the order of `photos`, only when the link is a FINALS link and its downloads switch is on (on by default; the reveal's `downloads` sets it at the send); a proofs link never has any. POST /v1/business/reveal-links/:id/downloads (E-274, body {on}) switches it and answers the link, whose `downloads` says which. Nothing before the passcode. The server makes no archive: the list is the download.

decisions.topic: Rename a shoot and a file (IB3)
decisions.decision: IB3: PATCH /v1/business/shoots/:id (E-277, {title?, client?}) and PATCH /v1/business/vault-files/:id (E-278, {name}) for the business's owner and its live logins; another business's shoot or file is 404, a removed login 403 login_removed. The new name shows in the shoot read, the Vault file list (E-214) and the download names; the stored object keeps its own key.

decisions.topic: Named files, plays and Vault tickets for logins (IB4, IB5, IB6)
decisions.decision: IB4: `files` (ids from the set, up to 200, in this order) on E-33 and E-272: left out, every ready file of the set; a file that is not a ready file of that set is 422 with words and nothing is taken. IB5: the first play of a reveal (after its passcode) sets the client wish's openedAt, a later play leaves it; each visit is one counted play; the shoot's reveal marks carry plays {count, first, last} and openedAt. IB6 (HU5): POST /v1/uploads (E-182) for the Vault purpose answers a live login (invited or active) of a business as it answers the owner, for that business (x-business-id names one when they hold several); a removed login is 403 login_removed, another business's login and a person of no business 403; a login's file goes with its shoot, under its own owner.

decisions.topic: Make the wish on a Concierge order (HZ2)
decisions.decision: HZ2: POST /v1/admin/concierge/orders/:id/wishes (E-273, {reason, kind, occasion, name}) for the order's own maker or the owner while the order is given or being made, up to the order's count: the wish is the buyer's (their account, and their business for a business's order), a draft tied to the order (wish.conciergeOrderId) and hidden from the buyer, from every list and read of theirs, until the order is delivered. The maker reads, saves, adds photos and seals it through the wish routes (E-224, E-225, E-226, E-231) while the order is with them, and loses it the moment it is delivered or the order moves to another maker; a seal on an order is paid by the order (a Signature ticket, no Pass or plan). E-34 delivers the wishes made through the order and the wishes named in wishIds (older orders); a delivery with none is 422. E-270 lists the order's tied wishes too. Cancelling the order erases a wish half made; erasing the buyer erases it with the rest.

decisions.topic: The ninth round's check: one reveal for a shoot and a client, links never more open than their reveal, hearts by file (IC1, IC2, IC3, IC5)
decisions.decision: IC3: for one shoot and one client there is one reveal. POST /v1/business/client-wishes/:id/send-reveal (E-33) answers 409 already_sent (fields sentAt and link) when that shoot's set already went to a client of that name, like POST /v1/business/reveals (E-272); its body takes `again` (boolean, optional) to send it once more on the same client wish, taking no second wish. A client wish made by E-30 is an ordinary client wish and takes its wish. IC1: a link copied for a shoot's set (E-153) carries the passcode, the downloads switch, the end and the switched-off time of the reveal it belongs to (the newest reveal sent on the set with a passcode, else the newest), whatever that reveal's state; sending again keeps the passcode and the downloads switch unless the body gives new ones. IC2: a heart belongs to a file: the link keeps the ids of the marked files, the wire still names positions in the link's file list (RevealPlay.index); a removed file's heart goes with it; sending again or copying again keeps the hearts of the files that stay. IC5: a play is counted for a link and an address in an hour, never from an id the page sends (the x-reveal-session header is not read); the 61st mark's 429 names the real wait; an Idempotency-Key used again for another shoot or client is 409 idempotency_key_reused.

decisions.topic: A wish is paid for once: one ticket payment waits per wish (ID1, HY1, HZ3, HU6)
decisions.decision: ID1: POST /v1/payments (E-87) for a ticket answers 409 ticket_payment_pending, with words and the fields `reference` (the waiting payment's) and `ticket`, while a ticket payment of that wish started by the same account still waits (pending or started, unfulfilled, and younger than the 60 minutes a waiting payment lasts); this holds for any ticket, the same one again with another Idempotency-Key included, and the same ticket with the same key still returns the same payment. Two starts at the same moment are lined up by the account lock: one payment waits, the other is 409. GET /v1/wishes/:id (E-224) carries `ticketPayment` {ticket, reference, startedAt, lapsesAt} for the owner (null when none waits; a maker reading a wish through an order gets null). POST /v1/payments/:reference/drop drops the caller's own waiting ticket payment at once, as HY1 does for plans: one conditional UPDATE marks it abandoned and flagged dropped_by_owner, so a new start is allowed; it answers the payment as it stands (E-88's shape); dropped again it changes nothing; a paid, failed or refunded payment is 409 ticket_payment_not_waiting; another account's payment or a payment that is not a ticket's is 404. A ticket payment that settles when the wish already holds a ticket that was PAID for (a purchase grant of kind ticket, not revoked, not refused) is refund due (refund_due:ticket_already_paid), whatever its state when it came in (waiting, dropped or lapsed: HU6, HZ3), whatever the wish's state; the payment's read says so in words, and the refund notice goes when it is refunded as for any refund. An extra bought twice (not the repeatable five-photos) is refund due the same way (refund_due:extra_already_held, with words). Both settles take the account lock then the wish lock, so two that settle at once give one ticket and one refund due, each with its ledger balanced.

decisions.topic: The buyer's files for a Concierge order (IC7, HZ2, IC4)
decisions.decision: IC7: POST /v1/uploads (E-182) takes the purposes order-photo and order-voice with subjectId the id of the caller's own Concierge order: the same signed put, confirm (E-184), screening, types and sizes as a wish's photos and voice; the files are the buyer's (ownerAccountId), tied to the order by a row of its own (concierge_order_file), from the moment the order is placed until it is delivered or cancelled (a ticket for an order that has ended is 409 order_ended; another buyer's order is 404). The limit that applies is the order's own: at most 20 photos and 3 voice notes per order (a file that has not been refused counts; the next ticket is 409 order_files_full with words); order files never count against the buyer's Vault, nor against the photo and voice limits of the buyer's own wishes. GET /v1/concierge-orders/:id/files lists the buyer's files for the order ({items: [{id, kind photo or voice, contentType, bytes, seconds, status, inWish, createdAt}], nextCursor: null, limits: {photos, voices}}); the buyer removes one with DELETE /v1/uploads/:id (E-183) while the order is open, and a file the maker already added to the wish being made cannot be removed (409 file_in_use). GET /v1/admin/concierge/orders/:id/files lists the same for the order's maker (the owner reads any order; a maker only the orders given to them; another maker's order, an order not given or not paid, and any other role are refused) and adds a signed read (url, expiresAt) for each file that is ready, null for one that is screening or refused. POST /v1/admin/concierge/orders/:id/wishes/:wishId/files {fileIds, reason} (the order's maker or the owner, while the order is given or being made) adds ready files of that order to the wish being made for it: photos join the wish's story photos and voice notes join its voices, under that wish's own limits (its ticket's, the Moment line when it has none); a file that is not the order's, not ready or not a file of this order is 422 with words; the files stay the buyer's and stay listed for the order; one audit row (concierge.add-files). Delivery keeps the files the wish uses with the wish and removes the rest (storage objects too); cancel (the buyer's or staff's) removes every file of the order and the half-made wish; the buyer's erase removes the files with the rest of the buyer's files; a refund leaves the order's files as the order stands (a refunded payment's order is cancelled by staff, which removes them). No one else reads them: a buyer reads only their own orders' files, a maker only orders given to them, and the order's files appear in no wish list of the buyer's.

The maker adds the files with E-280 under the Signature limits of each wish. IE2: an id in a request body is trimmed and, when it is a UUID, put in lower case before it is compared, stored or used as a key: POST /v1/payments (E-87) subjectId, so a start for the same wish in any spelling is one start (the others 409 ticket_payment_pending with the reference). IE3: the files given with an order that is never paid (placed or quoted) are removed, rows and stored objects, by the recurring upload-cleanup sweep once the order has not changed for LifecycleConfig.conciergeFilesDays (integer, 30, PROVISIONAL: the owner may change it; a price-book limit line limits.conciergeFilesDays set by PUT /v1/admin/prices/:key, DEC-252); the order stays. decisions.topic: A payment start names where the payer comes back to (IF1, HU1)
decisions.decision: IF1: POST /v1/payments (E-87), POST /v1/wishes/:id/keep (E-228, a keep, and a wake of a resting wish) and POST /v1/w/:slug/keep (E-257, the link holder's keep or wake) take an optional `returnPath`: a path on our own site. The server gives the provider the site's own address (PUBLIC_SITE_URL), that path and `?reference=<the payment's reference>` as the callback address (the stand-in provider's checkout address carries it as `?return=`); with no path the start is as before (the provider's own default callback). It is refused with 422 and the words in fields.returnPath, before anything is stored or asked of the provider, when it is: not text, 1000 characters or more, holding a control character, holding a backslash, not starting with one /, an address with a scheme, starting with // (another host), holding ? or # (the server adds the reference), holding an encoded slash, %00 or dot-dot, or a path the web does not serve for what is being paid for. Served paths: /app/wishes/return for any payment (the web's callback page reads any payment by its reference); a ticket, extra or keep: /app/wishes, /app/wishes/<the wish id> and, for a keep, /w/<a slug of that wish's link>; Concierge: /app/wishes; a plan or a pack: /app/pro/plan and /app/pro; vault space: /app/pro/vault and /app/pro; the Pass: /app/pass; the Studio's plan, signed, credit pack and extra review: /app/creator, /app/creator/studio and /app/creator/studio/<the subject id>; a link holder with no account (HU1): only /w/<the slug of the link they used>. The path is part of the request's fingerprint: the same Idempotency-Key with the same path returns the same payment, and the same key with a different path (or with a path where there was none) is 409 idempotency_key_reused: the first start's path wins and nothing is started again. A payment already open for the same order or plan that a start hands back keeps the path it was started with. The path is stored in the payment's request detail.

decisions.topic: Every route that takes an id answers a non-id in words and reads an id in any case (IF2, IE2)
decisions.decision: IF2: for every route whose path takes an id (the path parameters id, wishId, fileId, voiceId, creator and a payment `reference`: 97 routes of the registry), a spelling that is not an id is 422 with the parameter's name in fields and words ("Not an id: ...", "Not a payment reference: ..."), never 500 and never a bare 404; an id or reference in upper or mixed case is put in lower case before the route reads it, so the wish read, the payment read and drop by reference, the link routes and every other route read, drop and settle the same thing as for lower case. The check runs before the route's other validation (a global interceptor), after sign-in and role checks. A payment start whose subjectId is not an id is 422 {subjectId: "Not an id..."} (it answered 500). No endpoint or field changes.

decisions.topic: An extra is paid for once per wish as a ticket is (IF3, ID1)
decisions.decision: IF3: POST /v1/payments (E-87) for an extra answers 409 extra_payment_pending, with words and the fields `reference` (the waiting payment's) and `extra`, while a payment of the same extra for that wish started by the same account still waits (pending or started, unfulfilled, younger than the 60 minutes a waiting payment lasts); a different extra of the same wish, and the same extra of another wish, are not held up by it; the same key and body still returns the same payment; two starts at the same moment are lined up by the account lock (one payment waits, the other is 409). POST /v1/payments/:reference/drop (E-282) now takes a waiting extra's payment as it takes a ticket's: abandoned at once and flagged dropped_by_owner; a paid, failed or refunded extra payment is 409 extra_payment_not_waiting; the payment of any other purpose is 404. A paid-twice extra is still refund due (refund_due:extra_already_held, DEC-270).

decisions.topic: The contact route takes an Idempotency-Key
decisions.decision: POST /v1/support-threads/contact (E-254) takes an optional Idempotency-Key header (8 to 100 letters, digits or . _ : -; anything else is 422 in words). The same key and the same words (the address normalised, the subject and the message) is one thread: the first answers 201, a repeat answers 200 with the same thread and is not counted against the daily limits; the same key with another address, subject or message is 409 idempotency_key_reused and makes nothing; a different key is a different thread; no key behaves as before. Two starts at the same moment with one key make one thread. The key is kept only as a hash, with a hash of what was sent and the thread it made, in the new table support_contact_key (migration 20261202090000_contact_key_ab11a; removed with its thread).

Another order's files are not touched. No migration in prisma/migrations has a down script (none of the 31 before it has one), so the concierge_order_file migration is left as it is and no down script is added.

decisions.topic: A wish its owner removes can be brought back until a day, then it is erased (IF4)
decisions.decision: IF4: a wish its owner removes (DELETE /v1/wishes/:id, E-223) carries Wish.restorableUntil: the removal and the price book's restore days (30 today), kept on the wish. Bringing it back (POST /v1/wishes/:id/restore, E-230) before that instant works as before and clears the field; at or after it is 409 not_allowed ("The time to bring this wish back is over."), for every kind of wish (before this only a business's removed draft had a window). The erase job (the restore-window-end job, scheduled at the removal, cancelled by a restore) erases the wish when the day comes, whatever state it left: its content, name, passcode and maker's note are blanked, its link stays off and its slug loses the receiver's name, its file rows go and each stored object (with its sizes) is removed by one upload-cleanup job per file, and a business's draft gives its draw back. What a removed wish leaves: a paid ticket and a paid keep stay as payment records and the wish keeps its number and ticket kind (nothing is refunded by an erase; a link holder's email on a keep payment with no account is cleared); the voices friends gave through the gather link go with the wish (their names at once, their voice notes and files by the cleanup jobs; a voice the owner already put in the wish's content is a wish file and goes the same way); a reveal belongs to a business's client-wish record, not to the wish, so the erase only blanks the record's words (ZB3) and the reveal link keeps its own passcode and end. A wish staff took down (not the owner) has no window and is left alone by the job. Wishes removed BEFORE this change: their window starts at the migration 20261203090000_removed_wish_window_ab11b, which gives each owner-removed, not erased wish restorableUntil = the migration's moment plus the price book's days and schedules its erase job for then. It is the same link: the slug and the link path are the ones the link always had and no second link is made; the voices already given stay; the 12 a wish takes, the limits of asking per address and per link and the screening are as before. On twice, or on for a link that was never off, changes nothing and answers 200 with the same view (turning off twice stays 409 gather_off). Like /gather/off it has no rule about the wish's state, so it is allowed for a wish already opened: the view then says open false (a link takes voices only before the wish's first opening) and a friend's ask is still 409 gather_closed. decisions.decision: IF6: (1) GET /v1/showing (E-140) takes an optional `style` (a style's slug, any case): only the wishes listed in that style (the style they were listed in); a style nobody used is an empty page, a value that is not a slug is 422 in fields.style. (2) GET /v1/styles/:id/wishes (E-284, public): the wishes shown now in one style, by its slug or id; a style that is off or unknown is 404 as GET /v1/styles/:id answers. (3) GET /v1/creators/:handle/wishes (E-283, public): the wishes of a creator with a public page that are shown now. (4) GET /v1/creators/:handle/styles (E-285, public): the styles credited to that creator that are on, by slug, as the catalogue gives a style. A creator's profile itself (name, picture, line) stays GET /v1/creators/:handle (E-236, DEC-157), unchanged; E-283 and E-285 give it the wishes and styles the creator page draws. For E-283 and E-285 a creator whose account is suspended (an account ban in force), has no creator side (signed off) or is erased, and a handle that is not one, answer one 404, as E-236 does. Each read is paged as every list is (cursor and limit 1 to 50, default 20, nextCursor), reads through the live test of Now showing (a wish that is hidden by staff, resting, ended, removed, passcoded or not listed, or whose owner is banned or erased, is never in it), carries no viewer's mark (mine is empty) and no staff field, and is cached as the styles levels read is: ETag and Cache-Control public, max-age=0, must-revalidate (a 304 on a matching If-None-Match). decisions.topic: A Studio style's approved document plays at the wish's link and at the public style read (II1, HX4, HW2)
decisions.decision: II1: the document of a Studio style that was approved is given, typed as the creator's own read of the style types it (StudioStyle, `review` null), by the wish's link read of its style (GET /v1/w/:slug/style-files, E-266, which gains the field `document` beside `style` and `items`) and by the public style read (GET /v1/styles/:id, E-196, whose Style gains the optional field `document`; lists leave it out). decisions.topic: A refused file carries its reason in the server's plain words (II2)

No new kind is invented, and no customer text (a file name, a word in a photo) and no provider wording is passed through. The creator's list (E-267) and one-file read (E-268) now include a refused file, with status rejected, reason and no address. The stand-in screening's setting STANDIN_SCREENING takes an optional kind on a reject rule (reject:<part of a name>:<type-not-taken|empty|too-large|type-mismatch>; a hold rule takes none; any other kind is refused at boot); the screening result then carries that kind, so the verifier stack can drive every line. decisions.topic: Sample wishes are served as public reference data (IJ1)
decisions.decision: IJ1: GET /v1/sample-wishes/:kind/:occasion (E-288) answers the designed sample wish for a kind and occasion with no sign-in, in the shape the public wish read gives a player: kind, occasion, occasionName, receiverName, call, date (the text the designed source carries, e.g. 07 · 11 · 2026), opensAt (an instant already past, 7 Nov 2026), state open, openable true, content (the designed words), files ({role, url}) and photos (the site's own paths, /img/aisha-N.webp), and sample: true. It has no slug, wish number, owner, link, style or serverTime, so the answer never changes between reads. An unknown kind or occasion is 404 in words (the same for a kind and an occasion that do not belong together). GET /v1/sample-wishes?kind= (E-287) answers the samples of the named kind, or of every kind when none is named, as {items, nextCursor: null}: every sample is whole, at most 44 in one answer (the catalogue has 44 kind-and-occasion pairs; the largest kind, celebration, has 13). An unknown kind there is 404 in words; ?kind= left empty names no kind. Both reads carry the headers of the public reads (Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, and an ETag of the answer's own hash; a repeat with If-None-Match answers 304). Read only: any other method is refused.

decisions.topic: The sample wishes are a table the API owns, never a wish (IJ1)
decisions.decision: IJ1: the table sample_wish (model SampleWish, class config) holds one row per kind and occasion of the web's catalogue (44), seeded ONCE by scripts/export-seed-data.mjs from the web's sampleContent and SAMPLE_PHOTOS into prisma/seed-data/SampleWish.json and then owned here: the exporter writes that file only when it is absent and never reads those web files for it again (the files only it read are left out of SOURCE.json), so a later change in the web's adapt.ts changes nothing and fails no export check, as a style's get line. scripts/seed.mjs creates a row that is absent and never rewrites one; running it twice changes nothing. A sample is never a real wish: the table has no slug, owner, link, ticket or count column and is not joined to any wish table; it is in no wish list, count, report or Now showing; no route stores anything a person types in it (the two reads are the only routes), and every public wish route (/v1/w/:slug and its writes, /v1/showing/:id) given a sample's id answers 404.

decisions.topic: A secret opening is never sealed without its secret; the secret lives only as a hash (IK1, IK2)
decisions.decision: IK1: POST /v1/wishes/:id/seal (E-231), by every way a wish is sealed (a paid ticket, the Pass, a business plan, a Concierge maker on an order), answers 422 when the wish's opening is `passcode` or `question` and no secret is stored: fields.passcode and the message say "Set the passcode before you seal it." or "Set the answer before you seal it."; nothing is drawn or charged. PATCH /v1/wishes/:id (E-225): `passcode` is typed string or null (additive; null clears it, as its note always said); a save that names an opening with no secret, or changes the opening from one secret kind to another without a new `passcode` in the same save, clears the stored hash; content.opening.values never stores `code` or `answer` (the server drops them before the save, so a body that carries them is answered 200, not 500; hint and question stay) and no read returns them. IK2a: outer spaces are cut from a passcode and from an answer when it is set and when it is tried; 4 to 64 characters must be left (PATCH /v1/wishes/:id answers 422, fields.passcode and the message "Use 4 to 64 characters. Spaces at the start and the end do not count.", for a secret of spaces only or of another length); an answer is also matched in one unicode form (NFKC) and lower case ("Café" typed either way matches; lower case, not a full case fold, so "STRASSE" and "Straße" differ); a passcode keeps its case (an answer kept as typed before still matches as typed); 10 wrong tries an hour per address and the lock at 30 on the link are unchanged. No endpoint id is issued or changed; no field is renamed or removed.

decisions.topic: The portrait video is not sold without a renderer; the stand-in renderer; a ready video gives a signed address (IK3, IK4)
decisions.decision: IK3: POST /v1/payments (E-87) for extra.portrait-video answers 409 extra_not_sold (message "The portrait video is not on sale right now. Nothing was charged.", field `extra`) while no video renderer is configured, and makes no payment; the wish read's extrasOpen (DEC-306) says false for that extra; a wish that already holds the extra keeps the 503 video_unavailable on POST /v1/wishes/:id/video (E-148), now worded "Your video cannot be made right now. It stays yours and you will not pay again. Ask again later.". A second start for an extra the wish holds is 422 on subjectId ("This wish already has that extra.") and makes no second payment. PROVIDERS=standin binds the stand-in video renderer; the new setting STANDIN_VIDEO=fail makes every job fail, and is refused at boot with PROVIDERS=live or NODE_ENV=production; live providers keep no renderer until the real one is built (OWED, its own task). IK4: RenderJob gains the optional fields downloadUrl and downloadExpiresAt (E-147 and E-148): a short-lived (ten minutes) signed address of the stored file, only on the owner's own read of a done job; another person is 404, signed out 401. IK3a: the same 409 extra_not_sold (message "This is not on sale right now: it includes the portrait video, which cannot be made yet. Nothing was charged.") answers POST /v1/payments (E-87) for every line whose entitlements include the portrait video while no renderer is configured (the tickets whose grant says portraitVideo, Signature and Premiere today, read from the price book; the Pass, a business plan, a wish pack and a Concierge order, which hand out Signature wishes) and GET /v1/ticket-offers (E-213) for such a ticket. IK4a: an erased wish, or a video extra whose refund was sent, gives 404 on GET /v1/wishes/:id/video (E-147) and no address; the erase removes the stored video file with the wish's other files. Additive only.
